signals.name: Yield curve (10y-2y)
signals.reason_en: 10y-2y is +0.29pp (-0.21pp over 3 months, flattening): a flat curve moving toward inversion is bearish.
signals.rule: Inverted -> -1. Flat (0-0.5pp): flattening -> -1, steepening -> +1. Normal and steepening -> +1. Change measured over 3 months.

signals.name: Real 10y rate (10y - CPI YoY)
signals.reason_en: Real 10y = 5.04% yield - 3.7% CPI YoY = +1.32% (84th percentile of 10 years, rising over 3 months): liquidity is getting scarce relative to history.
signals.rule: Percentile vs last 10 years <= 25th -> +1 (abundant liquidity); >= 75th and rising over 3 months -> -1.

signals.name: Corporate credit spreads (CCC / BBB / AA)
signals.reason_en: CCC 13.61% (+3.26pp in 3m, 98th pct of 3m changes), BBB 1.17% (+0.17pp in 3m, 94th pct of 3m changes), AA 0.68% (+0.07pp in 3m, 84th pct of 3m changes). Spreads are widening: credit is pricing more default risk.
signals.rule: Each spread: 3-month change above its 90th percentile -> -1, below its 10th -> +1. Combined: two agree, or CCC widening alone ('junk moves first') -> -1. Moody's Baa-10y when ICE history is too short.

signals.name: M2 money supply
signals.reason_en: M2 +0.48% MoM (-0.1 sigma vs the 0.54% average since 1959), +5.7% YoY: within the normal range.
signals.rule: Month-on-month growth in the top 5% of months since 1959 -> +1 (abnormal liquidity injection); YoY < 0 -> -1; else 0. Read as confirmation of the bond-market signals.

signals.name: VIX
signals.reason_en: VIX 35.9 (98th percentile of 10 years, +20.8 over 3 months): volatility is high and rising.
signals.rule: Percentile vs 10 years >= 75th and up over 3 months -> -1; <= 25th -> +1; else 0.

signals.name: UMich consumer sentiment
signals.reason_en: Sentiment 51.5 (below trough zone, -0.2 in 3m); Expectations 52.9 (+1.4 in 3m): below 70 for 3+ months, consumers are pessimistic.
signals.rule: Expectations down >= 10 points in 3 months -> -1; several (3) readings < 70 -> -1; above 80 and not falling -> +1; else 0. Zones: 95-110 peak, 70-95 balanced, 55-70 trough.

signals.name: Building permits
signals.reason_en: Permits 1,295k SAAR, -8.7% YoY; 12-month average of YoY -1.8% (rising vs 3 months ago).
flags: Below the long-run trend band of 1.3-1.4m.
signals.rule: 12-month average of YoY growth > 0 and rising -> +1; YoY < 0 and the 12-month average falling -> -1; else 0 (rising/falling over 3 months).

signals.name: International money markets (Japan, UK, Germany, Italy)
signals.reason_en: Japan 0 (curve +1.53pp normal 0; real rate +0.65%, 88th pct, high, not rising 0); UK +1 (curve +1.61pp normal & steepening +1; real rate +1.64%, 95th pct, high, not rising 0); Germany -1 (curve +0.98pp normal 0; real rate +0.65%, 97th pct, high & rising -1); Italy +1 (curve +2.24pp normal & steepening +1; real rate -0.83%, 22nd pct, low vs history +1). Net +1: no clear message from abroad.
signals.rule: Each country read with the US template: curve (10y - short rate) and real 10y (10y - CPI YoY); country = the sign of the two. Net of the countries >= +2 -> +1, <= -2 -> -1, else 0. China shown, not scored.

texts.data_weak_price_up: Data vs prices: the bias is net short but the S&P 500 is in an uptrend (above its 200-day average and up over 3 months). Prices move before the reports: in 2019 and 2023 the market rose through weak data while the Fed reacted. Check what the market is pricing before going net short.
texts.data_strong_price_down: Data vs prices: the bias is net long but the S&P 500 is in a downtrend (below its 200-day average and down over 3 months). Prices may be discounting a slowdown the data does not show yet. Check what the market is pricing before adding net long exposure.
